name: Line of Control Valleys
inspired_by: The Kashmir Line of Control as of 2026: a river gorge valley crossing the LoC between Indian- and Pakistani-administered Kashmir, with Pir Panjal-type forested ridges, alpine meadows used by herders, a fenced and floodlit LoC with ridge-top posts on both sides, and a Kashmir-valley fringe of rice paddies, willow and apple orchards. After the April 2025 Pahalgam attack and the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, the LoC saw heavy shelling and drone use. A high north-east corner stands in for the routes toward Gilgit-Baltistan where Chinese-funded projects run. All towns are fictional.
climate: Humid subtropical in the lowest valleys (Koppen Cwa), temperate-continental in the valley (Dfb), alpine above 3,000 m. Valley summers 25-32 C, winters -5 to 5 C; heavy winter snow on ridges (passes closed November-May); 700-1,500 mm precipitation from western disturbances in winter and spring and monsoon fringe in summer.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Mar): deep snow on ridges, avalanches, LoC posts snowbound, chillai kalan cold in the valley
Spring (Apr-May): snowmelt, orchard blossom, passes reopen, infiltration season starts (historically)
Summer (Jun-Aug): herders on high meadows, monsoon showers, green valleys
Autumn (Sep-Nov): apple and saffron harvest, chinar leaves turn red, clear skies

vegetation: willow and poplar rows along canals
silver fir and spruce higher up
walnut and horse chestnut in ravines

terrain.relief: A deep river gorge (1,300-1,700 m) runs west across the map and through the LoC; steep forested slopes rise to ridges at 3,000-4,400 m with passes; the south-east corner opens onto the flat valley floor (1,550-1,600 m); a high plateau corner in the north-east above 3,500 m.
features: the LoC fence (double fence with floodlights and sensors) following ridges and crossing the gorge
ridge-top posts and bunkers on both sides
a river gorge with a few bridges and a crossing point (closed)
terraced maize fields on gorge slopes
a hydro project dam and tunnels on one side
terrain.water: A fast glacial river through the gorge, side streams and waterfalls, a hydro diversion dam, valley canals and a small lake on the valley floor; rivers freeze at the edges in winter.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Ridged multifractal Himalayan-type relief; gorge carved as a deep V-spline; valley floor in the south-east as a flat basin mask; north-east plateau mask. The LoC is a spline following ridge crests (via a ridge-finding pass) and dropping across the gorge; fence placed along it.
generator.erosion: Strong hydraulic erosion (120 iterations) for gullies; thermal cap 50 degrees; avalanche chutes as clear swathes in forest by slope and aspect.
generator.rivers: Main river spline through the gorge; tributaries by flow accumulation; valley canals on the floor.
generator.settlement_flattening: Gorge villages on terraces; valley villages flattened; posts on ridge crests.
generator.notes: Movement is channelled into the gorge road and passes; ridges dominate. The LoC fence and minefields are hazards; shelling events (both sides) create crater fields near posts. Helicopters limited by altitude and weather.

settlements.architecture: Kashmiri villages: two- and three-storey houses of brick in timber frames (taq and dhajji dewari construction) with pitched corrugated-iron roofs (often green or red) and attic storage, wooden balconies and lattice windows; mosques and shrines with pagoda-like tiered roofs; gorge villages of stone and timber on terraces.
settlements.wall_class: Brick-in-timber walls medium; stone thick; timber thin; LoC-side houses have bunkers (community shelters).
layout_rules: clustered on terraces or the valley floor around a mosque or shrine

settlements.architecture: District town: three- and four-storey brick and concrete buildings with tin roofs, a bazaar, a large mosque, army and police camps behind walls with sandbagged sentry posts, a bus stand, a hospital.
settlements.wall_class: Brick medium; concrete thick; camp walls thick.

settlements.architecture: Gujjar and Bakarwal herders' seasonal settlements: low mud-and-timber kotha huts with earth roofs dug into slopes, sheep pens, tents in summer meadows.
settlements.wall_class: Earth-sheltered huts thick on the uphill side.

settlements.architecture: Military and infrastructure: ridge-top posts with stone and concrete bunkers, sandbagged positions, overhead cover and nets; the LoC fence with floodlights; brigade camps in valleys; a hydro power project (dam, powerhouse in a tunnel, contractor camp); a road project with foreign engineers in the north-east.
layout_rules: posts on every dominant ridge point on both sides
fence 0.5-2 km behind the line on the Indian side

infrastructure.roads: One road through the gorge (to a closed crossing point and bridge), mountain roads with hairpins to posts, mule tracks to meadows and passes; a road-building project in the north-east.
infrastructure.power: Hydro project with dam and tunnels, power lines along the gorge.
infrastructure.airfields: Helipads at camps; AI aircraft only.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Army checkpoints on roads, the closed LoC crossing point, police checkpoints in towns.

pois.description: Post on a ridge crest: stone bunkers, trenches, overhead cover, a mortar pit, a helipad; facing posts within 500-1,000 m across the line.
pois.contract_use: observe only; shelling hazard; escalation objective

pois.description: Closed crossing point on a bridge over the gorge river: gates, a meeting hut, flags of both sides.
pois.contract_use: VIP or prisoner hand-over security (neutral); hostage hand-over

pois.description: Dam, intake, tunnel portals and a contractor camp with foreign engineers in a side valley.
pois.contract_use: protect infrastructure (client pak, Chinese-funded projects); hostage rescue of engineers

pois.description: Road-building camp with foreign engineers, machinery and a fenced compound on the north-east plateau road.
pois.contract_use: convoy escort (client pak, CPEC-type); protect workers

pois.description: LoC village after cross-border shelling: damaged houses, a crater in the school yard, villagers in community bunkers.
High pass with a herders' trail, caves and a cache spot; snowbound in winter.
pois.contract_use: high value target capture (client pak, on its side); intel recovery

pois.description: Hideout in deodar forest: a dugout with a camouflaged entrance, supplies, a radio set.
Gorge road blocked by an avalanche with trapped vehicles; snow-clearing machines.
Hillside Sufi shrine with an annual fair: crowds, stalls, pilgrims.
Crashed military drone in an apple orchard near the LoC; villagers gather.
pois.contract_use: recover a downed drone (client pak or neutral, depending on side)

pois.description: Valley camp with barracks, vehicle sheds, helipad and an artillery park.

conditions: valley fog and smog in winter
weather.visibility_notes: Snow and cloud close passes and ground helicopters; clear days give long views across the line; valley fog in winter mornings.
weather.dust_or_snow: Heavy snow November-April on ridges; no dust.

civilians.behaviour: Farmers and orchardists in the valley; herders move to meadows in summer; bazaars busy mornings; LoC villages use community bunkers during shelling and may evacuate; shrine fairs draw crowds. Strict security checks in towns.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: LoC villages and towns are sensitive; most contracts should avoid populated valley areas.

factions_present.where: Eastern half of the map (Indian-administered side): ridge posts, the LoC fence, valley camps and towns.
Western half (Pakistani-administered side): ridge posts, gorge villages, the hydro project and road camp.
North-east plateau corner only: engineers and company security at the road project (Chinese-funded projects); no PLA units (plausibility: the LAC with China is a different line).

frontline: The LoC is fixed; the war sim moves alert levels, not territory. Crisis events (attacks, retaliations, drone incursions, shelling) raise alert on both sides, post evacuation, recovery and infrastructure-protection contracts, and can escalate to artillery and drone exchanges along the ridges. India and Pakistan are mutually exclusive clients (long side-lock). India does not hire the player for operations inside Kashmir (per ind.json), so Indian-side contracts are limited to neutral humanitarian work; Pakistani contracts focus on project protection, HVT capture and hostage rescue on its side.
contract_hooks: Protect a Chinese-funded hydro project from attack (client pak)
Convoy escort on the road project (client pak)
Hostage rescue of kidnapped engineers (client pak)
High value target capture at a forest hideout (client pak)
Evacuate civilians from a shelled LoC village (neutral humanitarian)
Avalanche rescue and recovery on the gorge road (neutral)
Recover a downed drone from an orchard (client pak, on its side)

hot_zones.name: Gorge escalation (late game)
hot_zones.layout: Opposing brigade HQ in a valley camp (side set by the side-lock); 5 ridge posts as outposts; checkpoints on the gorge road; patrols and drones; artillery as a hazard; 1 QRF

insertion.fob: FOB at a host-side brigade camp (Pakistani side for pak contracts; a neutral humanitarian base in the valley for neutral contracts). Roads and trails; helicopters weather and altitude limited; no AAVs.

early_game_notes: State-on-state line with no faction-listed militant groups; mid-campaign. Militant attacks use generic hostile NPCs with no roster faction (Captain-confirmed 2026-10-10: no new faction).
captain_confirmed: map_size_km 20 x 20 km, within the confirmed 16-24 km per side (Captain, 2026-10-10)
hot zones are twice the area of a contract zone: 8-16 km2 vs 2-4 km2 (Captain, 2026-10-10)
